findings.title: Unused import of 'json' module
findings.description: The `json` module is imported at the top of operators.py but never referenced anywhere in the file. All JSON serialization is handled by diagnostics/report.py and diagnostics/benchmark.py, which maintain their own imports. This is a dead import that adds unnecessary module-load overhead.
findings.impact: Negligible runtime cost per load; clutters the import namespace and may confuse future maintainers into thinking JSON is used in operator definitions.

findings.title: Three viewport attribute-mode properties defined but never exposed in any panel
findings.description: The properties `surface_attribute_mode` (line 326), `particle_attribute_mode` (line 335), and `whitewater_attribute_mode` (line 346) are fully defined with extensive enum items in FLUIDSIM_PG_settings but are never drawn in any panel. A grep for `attribute_mode` across all panel files yields zero results. These represent UI surface area intended for color-by-attribute rendering that was either postponed or abandoned.
findings.impact: Users have no way to access these features through the UI despite the properties being registered. The properties occupy space in .blend files and registration overhead with no observable functionality.
findings.fix: Either wire these properties into the Output panel (FLUIDSIM_PT_output), or remove them from FLUIDSIM_PG_settings, or document them as programmatic-only API surface.

findings.title: Twelve IntEnum classes defined but never imported by any consumer module
findings.description: The following enums are defined in enums.py but are never imported by any other module: `MultiGridResolutionDecomposition`, `PressureDownloadProperty`, `ParticleAttributeDataType`, `FieldPrecision`, `Completion`, `ComputeAPI`, `DeviceType`, `CustomKernelType`, `CustomKernelFieldPermission`, `SourceVolumeType`, `SourceShapeNoiseSpace`, `GravityFieldsCombine`, `TurbulenceType`, `RampToScaleFieldType`, `TimeStepType`. These were ported for completeness from the synthesized enum tables but serve no runtime purpose.
findings.impact: Code bloat and maintainer confusion. A future developer may spend time investigating why these are unused. No functional impact at runtime.
findings.fix: Remove unused enum classes, or gate them behind a `__all__` with an explicit export list. Optionally move them to a `_legacy_enums.py` module with a deprecation notice.

findings.title: Empty sim/__init__.py forces deep import paths on all consumers
findings.description: The `sim/__init__.py` is completely empty (zero lines). Every consumer must write fully qualified imports such as `from fluidSim_warp_blender51.sim.fields import SparseGrid` rather than `from fluidSim_warp_blender51.sim import SparseGrid, FluidSolver`. This effectively treats `sim` as a namespace package, pushing import verbosity and tight file-name coupling to every calling module.
findings.impact: Increased import verbosity and tighter coupling to internal module file names. If modules are ever renamed or reorganized, every import site must change.
findings.fix: Populate `sim/__init__.py` with explicit re-exports of the public API surface (SparseGrid, FluidSolver, ParticleSystem, SolverSettings, constants, enums, etc.) to decouple consumers from internal file layout.

findings.title: FluidSolver is a God class violating the Single Responsibility Principle
findings.description: The `FluidSolver` class (spanning lines 484-1263, ~780 lines) owns topology management, grid-field lifecycle, source/collider descriptors, particle/whitewater systems, pressure/viscosity/surface solvers, snippet execution, profiling, statistics, and all per-substep orchestration. It is directly coupled to 8+ sub-module imports (kernels_core, kernels_fluid, pressure, viscosity, whitewater, surface, sourcing, custom). The single `step_frame()` method (line 1128) directly orchestrates 20+ private `_phase*()` calls in a monolithic loop with no extension points.
findings.impact: Extreme rigidity: changing the solver pipeline order, adding a new physics phase, or substituting a solver variant requires modifying the class body. Testing the orchestration requires instantiating the full GPU pipeline. The class cannot be extended without modification (violates Open/Closed principle).
findings.fix: Extract orchestrator phases into strategy or command-pattern classes (e.g., `TopologyManager`, `PressurePhase`, `ViscosityPhase`, `AdvectionPhase`). Have `FluidSolver` own a list of `Phase` objects and iterate them in `step_frame()`. This would collapse the ~20 private `_phase*` methods into a handful of phase objects.

findings.title: Global re-entrancy guard _LIQUID_VIEW_SYNCING is a fragile anti-pattern
findings.description: A module-level global `_LIQUID_VIEW_SYNCING` boolean (line 148) acts as a re-entrancy guard between `_apply_liquid_view_mode()` and `_sync_liquid_view_mode()` callbacks to prevent infinite recursion when two properties update each other. This pattern is fragile: it is not thread-safe (relevant for Blender background-mode rendering), may not reset correctly if an exception is raised inside the guard (the `try/finally` block is missing), and the global state persists across scenes.
findings.impact: If an exception occurs between setting the guard and resetting it, synchronization is permanently disabled for the session. In multi-scene or background-render contexts, the global flag could be erroneously set.
findings.fix: Replace with a context manager or decorator pattern that uses `try/finally` to guarantee reset. Alternatively, eliminate the mutual recursion entirely by coalescing the two callbacks into a single update function that checks which property triggered it.

findings.title: _probe_warp() called on every preferences draw() including Warp init
findings.description: The `draw()` method calls `_probe_warp()` unconditionally on every UI redraw. `_probe_warp()` calls `wp.init()` and queries device capability. On a slow or missing CUDA setup, these calls could block the Blender UI thread for hundreds of milliseconds on every redraw of the preferences panel.
findings.impact: Potential UI stuttering when opening or resizing the add-on preferences panel, especially on systems without CUDA where the Warp import or init may time out.
findings.fix: Cache the probe result with a timestamp-based refresh (e.g., re-probe only every 5 seconds). Move `wp.init()` into a one-time lazy init with a `_probed` flag.

findings.title: FluidSolver constructor allocates 25+ wp.array fields inline with no abstraction
findings.description: The `FluidSolver.__init__()` method (lines 487-550) directly creates every grid field, velocity component, temporary buffer, particle system, bin data, solver sub-object, and scratch array inline. This creates tight coupling between the orchestrator and every field's storage format. Adding a new scalar field requires modifying the constructor, the `_clear_grid_fields()` method, and potentially the `_remap` logic.
findings.impact: The solver's construction protocol is rigid and non-extensible. Any field addition or storage format change requires modifying the core orchestrator class rather than extending a field registry.
findings.fix: Introduce a `FieldRegistry` or `GridFields` container class that owns all field arrays and exposes them by name. Have `FluidSolver` own a single instance. This would also consolidate the 6-line velocity field allocation pattern into a single data class.

findings.title: Lazy-import _bridge() function duplicated across all operator execute() methods
findings.description: The `_bridge()` helper (line 11-14) provides deferred import of `scene_bridge`. It is called from every operator's `execute()` method, repeating the pattern 12+ times. This violates DRY and scatters the coupling to `scene_bridge` across the entire operators module.
findings.impact: Maintenance burden: if the bridge import path or API surface changes, every call site must be updated individually.
findings.fix: Promote the bridge reference to a module-level variable. Since `scene_bridge` has no bpy registration side effects at import time, a regular `from .blender import scene_bridge` at the top of operators.py is safe and eliminates all `_bridge()` call sites.

findings.title: Hardcoded compute phase name-to-label mapping duplicates constants.py knowledge
findings.description: The `names` dictionary (lines 423-431) in `FLUIDSIM_PT_diagnostics.draw()` maps compute slot indices (e.g., `compute_0`, `compute_1`) to human-readable labels. This mapping is related to `TIMER_PHASE_SLOTS` in `constants.py` (lines 69-86) but is independently hardcoded in the UI layer, duplicating phase-ordering knowledge.
findings.impact: If a new compute phase is added to `TIMER_PHASE_SLOTS` in constants.py, the panel must be updated separately or the new phase will not appear in the diagnostics UI. The two mappings may silently drift.
findings.fix: Replace the hardcoded dict with a reverse-lookup on `C.TIMER_PHASE_SLOTS` that generates labels from the phase keys. Add a `PHASE_LABELS` constant to `constants.py` as the single source of truth.

findings.title: VOXEL_UNUSED_1 defined but never referenced in any kernel or logic
findings.description: The constant `VOXEL_UNUSED_1 = 512` is defined in the voxel-type bitmask table but is never used, set, or tested anywhere in the codebase. Its name itself suggests it was intentionally unused, yet it remains in the canonical constants module.
findings.impact: Cosmetic clutter. A maintainer searching for available bits for a new feature cannot determine if `512` is reserved for external ABI compatibility or free for use.
findings.fix: Remove `VOXEL_UNUSED_1` or replace it with a comment at the end of the bitmask group: `# Bits 512+ available for extension`.

findings.title: RampToScaleFieldCombine enum values used as magic integers instead of enum references
findings.description: In `k_ramp_to_scale_field_volume` and `k_ramp_to_scale_field_particle`, the combine modes are hardcoded as integer literals: `if combine == 0:` (multiply), `elif combine == 1:` (max), `else:` (min). The `RampToScaleFieldCombine` enum class in enums.py defines these semantically but is never imported by kernels_core.py.
findings.impact: Magic numbers bypass the enum's documentation value. If the enum values were ever reordered or changed, the kernel would silently produce incorrect results.
findings.fix: Import `RampToScaleFieldCombine` from `.enums` and replace `0`, `1`, and the bare `else` with `int(RampToScaleFieldCombine.MULTIPLY)`, `int(RampToScaleFieldCombine.MAX)`, `int(RampToScaleFieldCombine.MIN)` respectively.

findings.title: Swap-buffer attributes named with opaque numeric suffix _position2, _velocity2, _attrs2
findings.description: The double-buffered scratch arrays are named `_position2`, `_velocity2`, `_attrs2` (lines 97-101). The `2` suffix is ambiguous: it does not convey whether this is a scratch, swap, next, or previous buffer. This reduces code readability, especially in `compact()` where ownership is exchanged via `self.position, self._position2 = self._position2, self.position`.
findings.impact: Moderate readability concern. A developer new to the codebase must study `compact()` carefully to understand the double-buffer swap semantics.

findings.title: Module-level import of contextlib placed inside a method body
findings.description: The `_phase()` method (line 593) conditionally imports `contextlib` inside a rarely-taken branch (`if self.profiler is None`). This places a standard-library import inside a method body when it could be at the top of the file.
findings.impact: Minor style concern. The import incurs a lookup cost on every invocation where the profiler is absent. Mostly a readability and discoverability issue.
findings.fix: Move `import contextlib` to the top of the file alongside other standard-library imports (after line 12).

findings.title: build_settings() is a monolithic 80-line property-to-dataclass mapping with no abstraction
findings.description: The `build_settings()` function (lines 64-143) manually copies every single property from the scene's property group into a `SolverSettings` dataclass -- an 80-line sequential block with no iteration or mapping table. The same manual pattern is repeated in `gather_sources()` (lines 201-263, 60+ lines) with field-by-field copying.
findings.impact: High maintenance burden: each new simulator knob requires manual wiring across three locations (properties.py field -> SolverSettings default -> scene_bridge.py copy line). The mapping is error-prone with no compile-time check that all properties are transferred.
findings.fix: Introduce an auto-mapping pattern: (a) have `SolverSettings` accept a property-group reference directly, (b) define a field-name mapping tuple iterated at module level, or (c) implement `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` protocols on property groups consumed generically.

findings.title: Sourcing module exceeds 1000 lines mixing GPU kernel definitions with registry boilerplate
findings.description: The `sourcing.py` module is 1021 lines long, containing 20+ Warp kernel definitions interleaved with 20+ `register_fn()` calls. The `register_fn(k_source_*, ...)` pattern after every kernel creates structural noise that obscures the kernel logic and violates single responsibility at the module level.
findings.impact: Low discoverability of kernel definitions amid registration boilerplate. The module is hard to navigate, jumping from kernel to registry call repeatedly.
findings.fix: Split into `sourcing/kernels.py` (pure GPU kernel definitions) and `sourcing/__init__.py` (registry wiring), following the same pattern as `kernels_core.py` / `kernels_fluid.py` which separate definition from orchestration.

findings.title: register() decorator is defined but never used; register_fn() is the sole consumer API
findings.description: The registry module exposes `register()` as a decorator factory (line 30) and `register_fn()` as a regular function (line 43). All 53 call sites use `register_fn()`. The decorator `register()` is dead code. Having both APIs creates ambiguity about which to use and why.
findings.impact: Unused decorator path adds module complexity and confuses new contributors who must parse both API forms.
findings.fix: Remove the unused `register()` decorator and rename `register_fn()` to `register()` to expose a single, simple API.

findings.title: Session class is a mutable data holder with no lifecycle protection or interface contract
findings.description: The `Session` class (lines 19-37) is a plain data holder without methods, mixing solver reference, profiler reference, frame statistics, validation results, benchmark data, error strings, and collider state. It is accessed as a module-level singleton via `session()`. There is no interface, no property validation, and no lifecycle state machine. Any module can freely mutate any field at any time.
findings.impact: Session state is unprotected: the solver can be set to `None` while panels read `sess.solver.grid`, causing `AttributeError` in the UI. There is no encapsulation of the session lifecycle (created, initialized, running, released).
findings.fix: Add lifecycle methods (`create()`, `release()`, `is_active()`), make fields read-only with properties, and protect against use-after-release with explicit state checks in accessors.
